original_record.why: The function supplies the hierarchy-orientation matrix used by the joint-rotation primitive that applies both solved corrections in the unit's two-segment inverse-kinematics routine.

links.rationale: Canonical local implementation independently supports this relation. Builds an output matrix from a joint-relative matrix and its ancestor chain. For each subject column, uses reciprocal magnitude above 1e-10 and otherwise the magnitude itself, then multiplies by the corresponding current joint-matrix column length. For ancestors, reciprocal normalization occurs above 1e-5; tiny columns instead multiply by their magnitude. Concatenates ancestor transforms into out. This is not guaranteed orthonormal or scale-free.

original_record.why: The function solves target angles for a two-segment articulated chain from joint positions, endpoint geometry, and segment lengths, then applies corrections to both JObjs.

links.rationale: Canonical local implementation independently supports this relation.
